text:
Alex: FYI I noticed the gitops CI attempted to automerge a bump to `modules/gpupool` but the pipeline aborted with a type-mismatch on the KMS input.
Maria: ugh. which change?
Alex: the module owner changed `kms_alias` from `string` to `object` to support regional alias maps. terraform plan fails during the apply stage: 
```
Error: Incorrect attribute value type

on modules/gpupool/variables.tf line 12, in variable "kms_alias":
 12: type = string

The given value is a map, but the variable is declared as a string.
```
Maria: that explains why automerge flagged it. did the PR have the compatibility note?
Tim: it didn't. CI labeler added `breaking-change` because the lockfile diff changed and the module schema hash bumped. InfraBot: Automerge blocked: label `breaking-change` present and `tf-plan` failed. See run: https://ci.redwood.internal/9887/logs
Jen: Is this just a schema change or will it force a canary rollback for running nodes? Cost/risk question — if gpupool can't read KMS correctly we may stop creating node credentials in eu-west-1.
Paul: Potentially risky. If the module expects a map now, any callers passing a string will get an apply-time error. That can fail terraform apply in production groups during a reconcilation.
Alex: Proposed mitigation: add a compatibility shim in the module to accept either string or map and normalize to map. Then bump patch version (semver patch) and update lockfile.
Maria: +1. Also gate automerge behind an extra step for any module with `kms` or `iam` changes: require `manual-approval` label on merges to main for 48h after PR.
Tim: can we do a more surgical fix? e.g., update the provider wrapper so existing callers are coerced: 
```
locals {
  kms_alias_normalized = can(regex("^\{.*\}$", tostring(var.kms_alias))) ? jsondecode(tostring(var.kms_alias)) : { default = var.kms_alias }
}
```
This avoids changing callsites.
Jen: clever, but brittle. If callers were relying on raw alias strings that match a region name, this could mask user errors. I favor explicit shim with a deprecation warning.
InfraBot: CI Action `module-lockfile` updated: file `module-lockfile.json` changed in PR #4238. Automated semver inference: breaking -> major, compatibility-shim suggested.
Paul: Also coordinate with regional capacity: eu-west-1 gpupool is near reservation cap. If we accidentally break reconciliation, autoscaler could overprovision fallback capacity in us-west and spike cost. Ops needs to be ready.
SRE Oncall: Oncall noted. If we plan to push a hotfix, schedule a 30m maintenance window and set a temporary read-only gating for controller reconciliation.
Alex: Plan: 1) revert automerge rule for module bumps that touch `kms`/`iam` to manual, 2) open quick PR with compatibility shim + deprecation warning, 3) run full canary apply against staging eu-west-1, 4) once stable, update lockfile and merge with manual approval.
Maria: I can own the manual approval and the canary apply. I'll also add a CI check to detect variable type changes in module diffs.
Tim: I'll draft the shim PR and include test cases in `modules/gpupool/tests/` to validate both string and map inputs.
Jen: I'll coordinate a short runbook for oncall if reconciler errors spike. Add metric alert on `gpupool.reconcile.errors` and `gpufleet.fallback.count`.
InfraBot: Reminder scheduled: `automerge` rule reverted for affected modules. Link: https://ci.redwood.internal/rules/453
Alex: Thanks — let's avoid accidental production scares. Once the shim is merged and canary looks clean we can re-enable selective automerge with a `no-breaking-kms` tag. :thumbsup:
Paul: FYI we should also check Dedicated customers with pinned module versions to ensure no hidden incompatibility.
Maria: noted, I'll message customers in the 48h window if necessary.
SRE Oncall: I'll be available during the canary apply window.
Alex: OK closing this thread — ping me if anything blocks the PR. :eyes:
